content.title: About
content.content: Popcorn is whole corn kernels that explode when heated, creating light, airy pieces. In movie theaters it is often served without added butter, making it less caloric while preserving its characteristic crunch and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Popcorn is the only type of corn that can "pop" due to its high internal moisture content.
The first commercial popcorn in the United States appeared in the late 19th century, and it became a cinema staple in the 1930s.
There are over 300 varieties of popcorn, but only about 30% are suitable for popping.
Butter‑free popcorn is usually seasoned with salt, caramel, or spices, but the plain version contains almost no fat.
In Japan, popcorn is sometimes flavored with soy sauce and sea salt.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Butter‑free popcorn contains minimal fat, making it a suitable snack for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: A serving provides a good amount of dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Corn kernels contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Popcorn provides thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Moderate glycemic index
items.content: Popcorn has a moderate glycemic index, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Popcorn is often salted; excessive sodium intake can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Small pieces can be inhaled, especially by children, so eat carefully.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to corn products.

items.title: Nutrient loss with additives
items.content: Adding sugar, caramel, or butter reduces the health benefits and increases calories.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Butter‑free popcorn is convenient as a standalone snack, at the movies, or at home. It can be seasoned with salt, spices, dried herbs, or a light sprinkle of Parmesan for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store popcorn in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage, keep it in the refrigerator to prevent moisture absorption, which can cause kernels to stop popping.
